---
title: "Circulatory disease deaths in Pennsylvania, 2018--2024"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
    theme: cosmo
    source_code: embed
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# data: one row per county and year
raw <- read_tsv("data/pa_circulatory_deaths_2018_2024.txt",   # tab-separated
                col_types = cols(`County Code` = "c"))         # GEOID as text

pa <- raw |>
  filter(!is.na(Year)) |>                        # drop the "Total" rows
  mutate(GEOID      = `County Code`,
         county     = sub(" County, PA", "", County),
         year       = Year,
         cases      = Deaths,
         population = Population)

# boundaries
pa_map <- counties(state = "PA", cb = TRUE, year = 2020,
                   progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326)                             # leaflet wants lon/lat

# one row per area: rate by county, all years pooled
by_county <- pa |>
  group_by(GEOID, county) |>
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), pop = sum(population), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(rate = 1e5 * cases / pop)               # per 100,000 person-years

my_map <- left_join(pa_map, by_county, by = "GEOID")

# join check
sum(is.na(my_map$rate))                          # should be 0
my_map$NAME[is.na(my_map$rate)]                  # which areas, if not

# one row per period: Pennsylvania by year
pa_year <- pa |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(cases = sum(cases), pop = sum(population), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(rate = 1e5 * cases / pop, area = "Pennsylvania")

focus <- "Lehigh"
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Circulatory disease death rate by county, Pennsylvania, 2018--2024 pooled

```{r map}
breaks <- quantile(by_county$rate, seq(0, 1, 0.2), na.rm = TRUE)   # quintiles
pal <- colorBin("YlOrRd", domain = by_county$rate, bins = unique(breaks))

leaflet(my_map) |>
  addProviderTiles(
    providers$Esri.WorldImagery,
    options = providerTileOptions(opacity = 0.5)
  ) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(rate), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 1,
    label = ~sprintf("%s: %.1f per 100,000 (%.0f deaths)",
                     NAME, rate, cases),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~rate,
            title = "Rate per 100,000<br>2018-2024",
            labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 0), opacity = 0.8)
```

> Rate = deaths / population over 2018--2024, per 100,000 residents per year. Darker red: more circulatory disease deaths per resident; five classes of about 13 counties each.

Column {data-width=400}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Death rate by year, Pennsylvania and Lehigh County, 2018--2024

```{r timeseries}
one <- pa |>
  filter(county == focus) |>
  mutate(rate = 1e5 * cases / population, area = focus)

cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Pennsylvania", focus))

p <- ggplot(bind_rows(pa_year, one), aes(year, rate, colour = area)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Rate per 100,000", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p)                                      # hover, zoom
```

> The Pennsylvania rate peaked in 2020 and then fell to its lowest level in 2024; Lehigh County (about 950 deaths a year) stays well below the state, with no clear change.

### Counties, 2018--2024

```{r table}
by_county |>
  transmute(County = county, Deaths = cases,
            Population = pop, Rate = round(rate, 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(Rate)) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

> Population is summed over the seven years (person-years).

AI statement 

I used Claude for parts of my code and debugging. It identified why my CDC WONDER file wouldn’t load (tab-separated text, not Excel) and it helped me adapt the lecture’s Ohio dashboard code to my Pennsylvania data,as some things were different and I was running into some code issues.I ran, knit, and checked the output myself.

### About these data

- **Outcome:** deaths from diseases of the circulatory system (ICD-10 I00--I99), 2018--2024, by year.
- **Population at risk:** residents of Pennsylvania's 67 counties (Census Bureau estimates, via CDC WONDER).
- **Rate:** crude death rate, deaths / population x 100,000; on the map and in the table, deaths summed over 2018--2024 divided by the population summed over the same years (person-years), an average annual rate.
- **Source:** [CDC WONDER, Multiple Cause of Death, 2018--2024, Single Race](https://wonder.cdc.gov/mcd.html); boundaries from the US Census Bureau, via `tigris`.
- **Areas without data:** none; no counts are suppressed.
- **Limitation:** the rates are crude, not age-adjusted, so counties with older populations (such as Cameron) look worse partly because of their age structure.
